page: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDSv4 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8272CL x86_64 processor operating at 2.6 GHz, providing 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled with 2458 GB of local SSD capacity, and the instance supports Premium Storage. No GPU accelerators are present on this configuration.

In benchmark testing, the D64ds_v4 demonstrates strong memory performance and database execution. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth reads reach 207.3 GB/sec, and writes achieve 95.23 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% of tested servers. Passmark database operations score at 22567.01, also indicating strong performance. CPU-intensive tasks, such as stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU extended instructions, show solid capabilities, though single-core execution remains in the average tier.

While the server handles standard compute and memory tasks efficiently, it exhibits performance limitations on highly specialized workloads. For instance, large-scale LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with text generation for a 70B model registering a poor score of 2.33 tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware. Consequently, the D64ds_v4 is best suited for general-purpose enterprise workloads, relational databases, static web serving, and software compilation rather than heavy AI model generation.
